desc:
Wix dashboard pages and site pages give your app a clear place for owners to set it up and, where needed, a public page on the live site. Ecom Swift LLC builds both with the Wix Design System, connected to your app data.

## What are Wix dashboard pages and site pages?

Dashboard pages are the screens inside the Wix dashboard where a site owner manages your app: settings, lists of records, setup steps. Site pages are pages on the live website that belong to your app, such as a landing page for a feature. Both are built as part of the app, and both can read and write the app's stored data.

## Why the dashboard is where an app is won or lost

Most owners never see your code. They see the dashboard. If it explains what to do, saves their changes and shows their data clearly, the app feels dependable. If it is confusing, slow or inconsistent, they conclude the app is too much work and remove it.

Site pages matter for a different reason. They are what the visitors of the owner's site see. A page that loads quickly, reads clearly and fits the site design makes the owner look good, which is why they keep your app.

## How these pages influence adoption and support

Well-made dashboard pages reduce the number of questions that reach your inbox. A form that validates entries prevents bad data. A table with search and filters lets owners find a record without asking you. An empty state that explains the first step prevents the blank-screen problem.

Clear pages also make it easier to grow. When owners can add, edit and delete their own records, you do not need to do manual work for them. Results depend on your app and audience, so we describe the pages we build, not the installs they bring.

## What good app pages include

- A page layout built from Wix Design System components, so it looks native.
- Forms with a save button wired to your data collection.
- Validation messages that explain what to correct.
- Empty states that say what the page is for and how to begin.
- Error states for failed saves or lost connections.
- Tables with search, filters and sorting.
- Add, edit and delete actions with confirmation for deletions.
- A first-run guide that walks new owners through setup.
- Bulk actions and CSV export for larger lists.
- Text prepared for translation, so languages can be added later.

## How we build the pages

We agree the page list and what each one lets the owner do, then draw a rough layout for approval. We build the pages in your repository, connect them to the data and test on a development site, including with no data, a small amount and a large amount.

The Basic package delivers one dashboard page with a form and save button wired to data. Standard delivers several pages with a searchable table, record actions, a first-run guide and one site page. Premium adds more pages, additional site pages, bulk actions, export, permissions for site collaborators and translation-ready text. If your backend does not exist yet, tell us, and we can connect to what you have or plan the data with you.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- List the tasks an owner must complete in the first session.
- Keep each page focused on a single purpose.
- Use plain words for labels, with no internal jargon.
- Test with a realistic amount of data.

**Avoid:**
- Putting every setting on one long page.
- Hiding the save button below the fold.
- Showing raw error codes to owners.
- Building site pages that duplicate what the dashboard already does.

## Who this is for

A developer with working backend code and no interface for it. A founder with a prototype whose pages look rough. An agency that needs a landing page and a settings area for a client app.

## What we need from you

A short description of what owners should be able to do, your data structure if you have one and collaborator access to your repository and Dev Center. We never need your password. Share any brand notes and the languages you plan to support.
